subject: Strategic tether: weekly readout — wins, risks, asks
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Oct 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Strategic tether: weekly readout — wins, risks, asks

Team — quick weekly dispatch ahead of QBR prep next week. TL;DR: momentum on throughput improvements, one customer escalation in scope and timeline risk, and three asks below. Attachments: QBR_readout_v2.pdf (slide draft), OKR_dashboard_oct_snapshot.png, SLO_latency_trends.csv.

Wins:
- Throughput optimization: Serving runtime kernel swap for seq-length 512 reduced p50 token latency by ~18% on Dedicated pools (see SLO_latency_trends.csv). This gains ~12% cost-per-token on our most common customer workloads (proof-of-concept rollouts scheduled).
- Sales motion: Acme Corp POC moved to pilot (non-prod) with a committed evaluation window after last week's demo; Sam Turner on cc. This is the highest-probability mid-market expansion this quarter.
- Observability: Console charts now surface prefix-cache hit rate per model, letting CS/SEs diagnose quality vs cost regressions faster.

Risks / Blockers:
- Data retention audit: Acme asked for a 7-year log retention clause for pilot (security redline). Legal flagged this as high touch; potential contract delay to procurement if we can’t scope retention exceptions.
- Capacity headroom: Spike testing on Dedicated shows sustained tail latencies if two large customers burst concurrently during peak. Current autoscale buffer covers average-case, but we need a temporary burst policy for QBR week.
- Eval regressions: A small regression (mean ROUGE drop ~1.6) on the summarization eval for quantized 4-bit v2 model when sequence length >1024. Research is investigating — may require model pinning for select customers.

Asks (action items):
1) Legal/Sales: Laura/Marissa — can you own the Acme retention conversation? Proposed immediate step: a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) limiting pilot to non-prod and logs retained only for 90 days for the pilot. I attached suggested language in the QBR_readout_v2.pdf (slide 6).
2) Infra: Jonas/Kimberly — recommend a temporary burst policy for Dedicated (2x ephemeral capacity for 48 hours around QBR dry run). Can you confirm cost delta and ops runbook by EOD Wed?
3) Research/Platform: Neha/Priyom — prioritize the summarization regression triage. If you can't reproduce by Thursday, propose pinning to 8-bit quant model for affected tenants and we’ll include notes in the QBR risks slide.

Planned sync: 30-min leadership huddle Wed 10/3 at 09:30 PT (calendar invite to follow) to finalize customer notes and the QBR risk slide. Please reply with terse status updates so I can consolidate the one-pager.

—
Rafael Mendes
VP, Platform & Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: [QBR_readout_v2.pdf (slides, 12 pages), OKR_dashboard_oct_snapshot.png (PNG, 1200x800), SLO_latency_trends.csv (CSV, 7KB)]

Thanks Rafael — I’ll take point on the Acme MAP. Initial thought: accept non-prod pilot with 90-day logs but request an SOC 2-sourced attestation on log handling. Laura and I will draft the MAP and send a short redline to Sam by EOD Tue.

Marissa

Rafael — I ran the numbers on a temporary burst policy. Quick summary:
- 48-hour 2x ephemeral burst for the Dedicated pool estimated incremental cost: ~$18k (one-time) for our current fleet mix.
- Ops runbook draft: auto-warm GPUs 2 hours prior to scheduled dry-run; graceful fallback to host-model variants on sustained >5% tail latency.

We can commit to the burst policy if leadership approves. I’ll attach a short cost breakdown to the calendar invite.

Jonas
Director, Infra

I’ll join the Wed huddle and bring the one-page MAP draft so we can finalize.
